summary.note: kind_accuracy is the defensible headline: it asks whether the labeller identified WHAT the asset is, and the game's table answers the same question. use_accuracy is weaker by construction - the labeller tags an asset's apparent function while the table records which subsystem consumes it, and a skill icon reused by a rune or state row makes those two answers differ without either being wrong. The single_table / shared_icon split below was added to test whether shared icons explain the gap. They do not: single-table clusters score LOWER on use, so the ~0.6 figure reflects the apparent-function vs consuming-subsystem mismatch across the board, not duplicate reuse. Read use_accuracy as agreement between two different axes, not as an error rate.
